decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.

changes.quote: The war and related events are contributing to upward pressure on inflation and are weighing on global economic activity.
changes.explanation: The Fed slightly softened its phrasing on how international conflicts add to inflation pressures.

changes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: The target range for borrowing costs was adjusted upward to reflect the new policy rate.

tone_quotes.quote: Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher food and energy prices, and broader price pressures.

The Committee anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 16.27% APR, a 50 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.49% and moved -2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.49% would fall by about $3.94 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 3.6%, and employers added an average of 293k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 7.1% over the past year (November 2022); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 5.3%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +1 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.61%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.02% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that policymakers expect further rate increases will be needed to bring inflation back down to 2 percent. An educational forecast model assigned a 96% probability to a hike at the next meeting.
